title: Mumbai offshore — Indian EEZ

gallery.blurb: A pipeline, a platform, a ship that isn't broadcasting. Before naming anyone — what kind of thing did this?

notes: The source-classification case: the answer here may not be a vessel at all. Target acts: detect, trace, attribute, verify. Export box 72.0863 18.4023 72.2678 18.6072, 100% inside the scene footprint, dB clamp [-28, -15]. The scene shows several bright point targets near the slick head — real radar returns for the ship detector, not speckle. cerulean_slick.geojson is Cerulean slick 3612640 (20.55 km, 7.74 km2, model confidence 0.928). ais_source is gfw_hourly — one position per vessel per hour against NOAA's ~71 s, so Stage 3's 'gap' component is structurally impossible and 'slowdown' is very coarse. Both must come back null, never 0 (Master §6.1, D20). CORRECTION TO EARLIER PLANNING DOCS: the 'known natural seep area' warning attributed to Cerulean could NOT be substantiated — their API exposes four AOI layers (EEZ, IHO sea areas, Marine Protected Area, user-generated) and no seep layer, and this slick is classed VESSEL, not NATURAL. Do not render a natural_seep flag on this case until somebody produces the source.
